About Tekion

Positively disrupting an industry that has not seen any innovation in over 50 years, Tekion has challenged the paradigm with the first and fastest cloud-native automotive platform that includes the revolutionary Automotive Retail Cloud (ARC) for retailers, Automotive Enterprise Cloud (AEC) for manufacturers and other large automotive enterprises and Automotive Partner Cloud (APC) for technology and industry partners. Tekion connects the entire spectrum of the automotive retail ecosystem through one seamless platform. The transformative platform uses cutting-edge technology, big data, machine learning, and AI to seamlessly bring together OEMs, retailers/dealers and consumers. With its highly configurable integration and greater customer engagement capabilities, Tekion is enabling the best automotive retail experiences ever. Tekion employs close to 3,000 people across North America, Asia and Europe.

Director, GTM Engineering

Reports to: SVP of GTM & Growth
Location: Bay Area preferred

"This isn't a traditional GTM Engineering role. It's a commercialization architect role responsible for building the systems, automation, workflows, and operating model that will help Tekion turn product innovation into scalable revenue growth."

Job Introduction

GTM Engineering is an emerging function that sits between Revenue Operations and Software Engineering. This person designs, builds, and operates the data pipelines, enrichment workflows, AI agent deployments, and automated plays that the GTM team runs on. Every major SaaS company scaling AI-assisted GTM motions in 2026 is hiring for this role — it is the operational backbone that makes distribution, sales, and CS teams significantly more productive.

At Tekion, the Director of AI Distribution will build the campaign engine. The Director of GTM Engineering makes that engine — and every other GTM workflow — faster, smarter, and more automated. They define, deploy, evaluate, and optimize AI agent workflows across the GTM org: lead enrichment, outbound personalization, campaign QA, call prep, competitive intelligence, and pipeline analytics.

Key Role & Responsibilities

AI agent workflow design and deployment across GTM — selecting, configuring, and orchestrating agents for lead enrichment, outbound personalization, content generation, campaign QA, and call preparation
GTM tech stack architecture and optimization — owning the integration layer across HubSpot, Salesforce, Databricks, Clay, and emerging AI tooling
Automation of repetitive GTM workflows — replacing manual processes with agent-driven or rule-based systems that scale without adding headcount
Evaluation and QA of deployed agents — monitoring output quality, measuring impact on conversion rates and pipeline velocity, and iterating based on data
Data pipeline and enrichment infrastructure — ensuring GTM teams have accurate, real-time data on accounts, contacts, intent signals, and competitive positioning
Internal tooling and dashboards — building the operational views that let GTM leadership see pipeline health, campaign performance, and agent effectiveness in real time

What This Person Does NOT Own

Campaign strategy, messaging, or creative — that belongs to the Director of AI Distribution and GTM leads
Product engineering or platform infrastructure — this role builds on top of Tekion's platform, not inside it
Sales execution or quota — this role makes sellers more effective, not more numerous
Marketing brand, events, or content strategy — this role automates distribution of content, not creation of it

Basic Qualifications

5–8 years in GTM operations, revenue operations, growth engineering, or sales operations — with a strong technical/builder orientation
Has personally built and shipped automation workflows using tools like Clay, n8n, Zapier/Workato, or custom scripts — not just managed vendors who did it
Deep fluency in AI agent frameworks — understands how to prompt, chain, evaluate, and monitor AI agents in production GTM workflows
Strong data engineering instincts — comfortable with SQL, API integrations, data pipelines, and can work alongside engineering teams without being one
Experience with CRM architecture (Salesforce), marketing automation (HubSpot/Marketo), and enrichment platforms (Clay, ZoomInfo, Apollo)
Systems thinker who sees GTM as an interconnected machine, not a collection of point tools
Has operated in a high-growth B2B SaaS environment where speed of iteration mattered more than perfection
Comfortable being the first hire in a new function — can define the role, build the roadmap, and execute without waiting for direction

First 90 Days

GTM tech stack audit complete — map of current tools, integration gaps, and automation opportunities documented
First 3 agent workflows deployed and in production (e.g., lead enrichment, outbound personalization, campaign QA)
Measurable time savings quantified — hours saved per GTM team member per week from automation
Data pipeline improvements — enrichment coverage increased, lead-to-account matching accuracy improved
Dashboard or reporting layer built that gives GTM leadership a real-time view of agent performance and pipeline health

Reporting Structure

Both roles report directly SVP of GTM & Growth. They sit alongside Director of GTM and the five GTM leads (Fixed Ops, Retail, Accounting, T1, OEM/Integrations). The Director of AI Distribution and the Director of GTM Engineering are peers — not a reporting chain.

Perks & Benefits

Competitive compensation and generous stock options
100% employer-paid top-of-the-line medical, dental and vision coverage
Great benefits including unlimited PTO, parental leave and free snacks and beverages
The opportunity to work with some of the brightest minds from Silicon Valley’s most dominant and successful companies
Be part of an early stage, hyper-growth start-up with the opportunity to grow and prosper
Work on the latest and coolest technologies – everything is home-grown and built ground-up
A dynamic work environment with a strong sense of community and collaboration
The open and transparent culture that encourages innovation, rewards performance and discourages hierarchy
Exciting opportunities for career growth and development

Reports to: Director of Detection Engineering and Threat Hunting

Location: Remote, US

Compensation: $220,000 to $240,000 base plus bonus and equity

What We Do:

Cybercrime is growing, and more businesses are getting hit by threats that used to target only the biggest organizations. That pushes defenders like us to operate at the highest level, and it deepens our need for good people who want to make a meaningful impact.

Founded in 2015 by former NSA cyber operators, Huntress is a remote-first team working to make enterprise-grade cybersecurity accessible to businesses of all sizes. We work closely with security teams and service providers protecting complex environments, often without the time or headcount to handle it all. That’s why we build our technology in-house and back it with a 24/7 human-led Security Operations Center (SOC). As a result, our platform is never disconnected from the experts who manage it, ensuring our customers' protection.

Huntress now secures more than 5M endpoints and 11M identities worldwide. Those numbers keep growing because more businesses rely on us to help carry the load and operate with more confidence. Every day, you can see that commitment in how we stand with our customers and how we show up for each other.

What You’ll Do:

We are seeking an experienced leader to own the strategy, execution, and growth of our North American
Detection Engineering & Threat Hunting (DE&TH) operations.

While you will align with the DE&TH Director on the overarching 18-month vision, you will have autonomy to drive the operational tempo and outcomes for your region. You will provide weekly supervision to focus on scaling the team, managing regional hiring/budgeting, and serving as a strategic partner to Product and Engineering.

You will manage a team of technical practitioners. Your mission is to operationalize our "hunt-to-detect" feedback loop at scale, ensuring that our detection portfolio matures in lock-step with our platform's growth, while collaborating with your counterparts in other regions to ensure a seamless, 24/7 global defense.

Responsibilities:

Regional Operational Leadership: Own the execution of the DE&TH mission for the North America region. You will translate global strategic goals into actionable regional roadmaps, ensuring that our NA-based hunters and engineers are focused on the highest-value threats.
Team Scaling & Talent Strategy: Manage and grow a team of practitioners. You are responsible for the region's hiring strategy, capacity modeling, and performance management. You will mentor up to Staff and Principal practitioners, helping them navigate technical leadership paths.
Cross-Functional Alignment: Strategize with leaders in Product, Engineering, and Security.
Global Collaboration: Partner closely with regional managers in EMEA/APAC to ensure consistent standards, seamless handoffs, and shared knowledge. You will ensure that "how we hunt" in North America contributes to and benefits from our global ecosystem, preventing regional silos.
Incident Command: Serve as the senior leadership point of contact for DE&TH during North American business hours. During high-impact security incidents or mass exploitation events, you will provide calm, strategic direction to the team and effective communication to executive stakeholders.

new_jobs.title: Chief Product Engineer - Audio Technology
new_jobs.description:
At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound.

Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation.

Job Description

The Chief Product Engineer
serves as the top technical leader responsible for aligning product engineering with product, intellectual property (IP) and licensing strategies. This role bridges core research and development (R&D) with external commercialization, ensuring that engineered systems are modular, documented, and legally robust for third-party adoption or joint ventures. As the principal technical architect responsible for the creation, protection, and commercial transfer of our proprietary consumer audio and hearables technology
. You will ensure that our patented algorithms, hardware / software architectures, and software stacks (e.g., ANC, spatial audio, voice pickup, wireless connectivity) are packaged into robust, modular, and easily integrable Reference Designs or Intellectual Property (IP) blocks for third-party consumer electronics brands and ODMs.

Key Responsibilities

Licensing Architecture Strategy: Define and design the technical boundaries of our licensing portfolio (IP blocks, SDKs, reference hardware). Ensure audio technologies are modular and seamlessly integrate into diverse host chipsets (Qualcomm, Bestechnic, MediaTek, etc.).
DSP Platform Integration: Oversee the optimization and integration of audio code libraries across leading wireless audio SoC and DSP platforms (e.g. Cadence Tensilica HiFi DSPs etc.).
Technical Package Delivery: Oversee the development of comprehensive Technical Data Packages (TDPs). This includes golden reference designs, tuning tools and software, comprehensive SDKs, APIs and bit-exact reference models, acoustic design guidelines, DSP code libraries, and documentation for licensee onboarding.
Tuning & Tooling Development: Champion the creation of developer-facing software tools and GUI-based tuning utilities that empower licensees to calibrate ANC, EQ, and spatial audio parameters to their specific acoustic hardware.
Partner Evaluation & Integration Support: Act as the primary technical authority during licensing evaluations. Provide deep-dive technical support, reference tuning, and architectural reviews for tier-1 consumer electronics licensees and manufacturing partners (ODMs).
IP Protection & Compliance: Partner with the Legal and IP teams to identify patentable innovations in hardware, firmware, and acoustic architectures. Develop technical validation methodologies and tools to audit and verify licensee compliance.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Mentor a highly specialized team of audio, DSP, firmware, and hardware engineers, steering their R&D output toward scalable, high-margin licensing platforms rather than single bespoke products.

Required Skills & Qualifications

Experience: 12+ years in consumer audio, acoustics, or hearables product development (e.g., TWS earbuds, smart headphones, spatial audio systems), with a heavy emphasis on embedded software and DSP algorithm development. At least 4 years managing software IP delivery, technical transfers, or external licensing integrations.
Algorithm & DSP Mastery: Deep expertise in developing and optimizing real-time audio processing software. This includes fixed-point math optimization, assembly-level vectorization (e.g., NEON, Tensilica instruction extensions), and low-latency scheduling.
Domain Expertise: Domain mastery over core hearable software pillars: Active Noise Cancellation (ANC/biquad design), Spatial Audio/HRTF, Echo Cancellation (AEC), Wind Noise Reduction, and Machine Learning-based Voice Pickup (VPU). Deep understanding of Bluetooth LE Audio/Auracast, microphone arrays (beamforming), and audio codecs (LC3, LDAC, aptX).
Systems & Standards: Strong fluency in C/C++, Python (for modeling), real-time operating systems (RTOS), Bluetooth LE Audio pipelines, Auracast, and standard audio codecs (LC3, AAC, LDAC).
Hardware & Acoustic Context: Solid understanding of how software interacts with physical acoustic constraints, including microphone array geometries, transducer frequency responses, and ADC/DAC latency paths.
Communication & Negotiation Support: Exceptional ability to present highly complex acoustic and software concepts to non-technical business stakeholders, IP attorneys, and external executive teams.
Education: Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Acoustical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

Our compensation is thoughtfully tailored to your skills, experience, education, and location, and goes beyond base salary. Reporting to the VP of Data & AI, this Director manages a team of Data Engineers and Database Administrators, chairs the cross-functional Data Governance Council, and partners across Products, Infrastructure, Legal, and Compliance to position data as a strategic enterprise asset. Data Engineering Leadership & Team Management

Lead, mentor, and develop a team of Data Engineers and Database Administrators responsible for Fintech's data infrastructure
Drive technical excellence in data engineering practices, establishing coding standards, review processes, and operational runbooks
Manage capacity planning, project prioritization, and resource allocation across concurrent initiatives including platform evolution, product delivery, and operational maintenance
Build a high-performing, collaborative team culture aligned with Fintech's collective intelligence philosophy

Database Operations & Platform Management

Oversee operations and optimization of the enterprise database portfolio:
PostgreSQL: Primary transactional database supporting modernized applications
Apache Druid: Real-time analytics and OLAP workloads
MongoDB: Document store for flexible schema requirements
OpenSearch: Search, logging, and observability

Establish database performance monitoring, capacity management, and incident response procedures
Drive continuous optimization of cloud-native database deployments for cost, performance, and reliability
Partner with Infrastructure on Azure cloud optimization, Kubernetes deployment patterns, and Terraform infrastructure-as-code for data resources

Data Pipeline Architecture & Operations

Own the design, development, and maintenance of enterprise data pipelines spanning:
Ingestion: Apache NiFi for batch/file processing, SFTP integrations with trading partners
Streaming: Apache Kafka for real-time event pipelines
Processing & Storage: Databricks lakehouse as the enterprise source of truth with Unity Catalog governance
Distribution: Pipelines feeding fit-for-purpose downstream databases and third-party integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, Chameleon, Heap)

Establish pipeline observability, alerting, and SLA management across the data stack
Drive adoption of DataOps practices including CI/CD for data pipelines, automated testing, and deployment automation

Data Contracts & API Development

Define and implement the enterprise data contract framework—formalizing schemas, quality expectations, SLAs, and ownership for data exchanged between producers and consumers
Partner with API/MDM team to design and deliver data APIs via KrakenD gateway, ensuring consistent access patterns and rate limiting
Establish schema registry and versioning practices for Kafka topics and Databricks tables
Integrate data contracts into the SDLC, ensuring contract validation at pipeline deployment

Data Governance Program Leadership

Establish and chair the enterprise Data Governance Council with representation from Data, Products, Infrastructure, Legal, and Compliance
Design and operationalize the enterprise data governance framework grounded in DAMA DMBOK, covering:
Data quality standards and measurement
Data classification and sensitivity labeling
Access control policies and enforcement
Retention and archival requirements
Lineage and impact analysis

Implement governance controls natively within Databricks Unity Catalog—including catalog/schema/table permissions, row/column-level security, and attribute-based access via integration with CRAFT (zero-trust ABAC layer)
Lead metadata management using Open Metadata integrated with Unity Catalog, ensuring comprehensive lineage from source systems through consumption
Maintain the enterprise business glossary with consistent definitions across all 12 product lines
Recruit and coordinate federated Data Stewards and Data Owners across business units

Data Security & Protection

Own the data security posture across the enterprise data platform, partnering with Information Security to implement defense-in-depth controls
Implement and monitor data-at-rest encryption (Azure Storage encryption, Databricks workspace encryption) and data-in-transit encryption (TLS for all data movement)
Establish data masking, tokenization, and anonymization standards for sensitive data elements (PII, PCI, financial data)
Configure and maintain Unity Catalog audit logging and system tables for comprehensive data access monitoring
Define and enforce least-privilege access models across all data platforms, integrating with Auth0 identity and OPA policy enforcement
Lead data security incident response procedures, including breach investigation, impact assessment, and remediation
Conduct periodic data security risk assessments and vulnerability remediation

Certification, Audit & Regulatory Compliance

Serve as the data engineering and governance lead for SOC 2 Type II certification, ensuring data-related controls are documented, implemented, tested, and auditable
Align governance and security controls with NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF 2.0), particularly:
Govern: Risk management strategy, roles/responsibilities, policy
Identify: Asset management, data inventory
Protect: Data security, access control, platform security
Detect: Continuous monitoring via Unity Catalog audit logs

Prepare governance documentation and evidence collection for NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation (23 NYCRR 500) requirements—access controls, audit trails, third-party data risk management, and incident reporting
Ensure CCPA compliance through governance processes supporting data subject rights (access, deletion, portability) with technical implementation in the data platform
Partner with Legal on 50-state alcohol regulatory data requirements, ensuring proper retention and auditability for licensing compliance
Conduct annual data governance maturity assessments and develop continuous improvement roadmaps

AI & Advanced Analytics Enablement

Establish data engineering and governance foundations for Fintech's AI platform including:
Training data lineage and provenance documentation
Feature store governance and access controls
Model input/output data quality monitoring

Partner with Data Architecture on vector and graph database integration patterns for AI workloads
Monitor evolving AI governance requirements (NIST AI RMF, SEC AI disclosure guidance, NYDFS AI risk guidance) and advise council on data governance implications
Ensure AI training data complies with data classification, consent, and regulatory constraints

Strategic Planning & Stakeholder Engagement

Develop and execute the multi-year data engineering and governance roadmap aligned with Fintech's platform strategy and 3-year ecosystem vision
Translate technical data initiatives into business value for executive stakeholders
Manage vendor relationships for data platform tooling (Databricks, Confluent/Kafka, OpenMetadata)

Represent Data Engineering & Governance in cross-functional initiatives including M&A integration, new product launches, and enterprise architecture reviews

Qualifications

Required Education:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field

Required Knowledge And Experience

10+ years of progressive experience in data engineering, data management, or related technical disciplines
